title: Ramp-and-sustain load probe for Dedicated Capacity: quantile SLAs, autoscale trigger validation, and customer handoff checklist
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a reproducible ramp-and-sustain load probe and benchmarking playbook for Dedicated capacity that measures throughput guarantees and validates autoscaling triggers and fleet control behavior under realistic, customer-like traffic shapes. This ticket covers harness implementation, quantitative measurement methodology (including per-quantile tail analysis), and the customer acceptance checklist for handoff to Solutions/Onboarding teams.

Goals:
- Produce a reusable load harness that can run ramp, sustain, spike, and chaotic-noise scenarios against a Dedicated pool.
- Define clear benchmarking methodology: request/response distributions, warm-up/KV cache priming, statistical significance, and quantile reporting (P50/P90/P95/P99/P99.9).
- Validate autoscaling policy semantics (scale-up latency, scale-down hysteresis, max burst handling) with deterministic tests.
- Validate fleet controls: model fallback, region fallback, and reserved slot exhaustion behavior.
- Create a customer-facing acceptance checklist and report template that Solutions can use during onboarding.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change autoscaler implementation or SLA language. It focuses on measurement and validation.

Proposed approach:
1) Harness: implement a step-based driver that can replay synthetic traces with configurable per-request token lengths, inter-arrival distributions (Poisson, bursty), and KV cache priming sequences. Use existing prober infra but add: sustained-phase duration, programmable ramp slopes, and built-in quantile collectors.
2) Bench methodology: run N=5 independent runs per scenario; discard first warm-up window; compute median and 95% CI for throughput and latency quantiles; also compute error-rate and tail-latency variance across runs.
3) Autoscaling validation: create deterministic step-up tests that push utilization past scale thresholds and measure time-to-target and overshoot. Create step-down tests that ensure hysteresis prevents flapping.
4) Fleet controls: simulate a simulated-exhaustion event (mark reserved slots full) and validate that policy falls back to pre-configured model variants or returns controlled error codes per policy.

Measurement methodology details:
- Metrics to capture per-request: model, sequence_length, tokens_in, tokens_out, queue_time_ms, inference_time_ms, total_latency_ms, responder_node, cache_hit(boolean).
- Aggregation windows: 10s windows for ramp, 60s windows for sustain.
- Report items: throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec), success rate, P50/P90/P95/P99/P99.9 latencies, 99.9th tail spike counts, autoscale events (timestamp/target_size), and KV cache hit-rate.
- Statistical rigor: use bootstrap on per-request latencies to estimate 95% CI for each quantile.

Test scenarios (examples):
- Ramp-to-sustain: linear ramp from 0 to target_rps over 5 minutes, sustain 30 minutes, ramp down. Target_rps will be set per-customer signature (e.g., 500 rps, 2k rps).
- Spike + recovery: sustained baseline at 30% of capacity, 10s spike to 300% to validate burst handling and queuing behavior.
- Stateful KV-primed: run priming workload that warms KV cache for top-20 prefixes, then replay customer-like sequences to measure hit delta.
- Chaos-noise: interleave small random request storms (exponential inter-arrival) to ensure autoscaler noise resilience.

Autoscaling validation checklist:
- Trigger threshold test: verify scale-up is initiated when CPU/GPU-util or internal QPS proxy crosses configured threshold within TTL.
- Scale-up latency: measure time from trigger to first additional worker ready and contributing to throughput.
- Scaling granularity: ensure increments align with pool sizing config.
- Scale-down hysteresis: validate no flapping by enforcing minimum cooldown.

Fleet control checks:
- Model fallback: when primary model variant returns capacity error, assert fallback path is chosen and responses still meet degraded SLA.
- Region fallback: simulate regional failure and verify controlled routing to backup region and TTL for routing decisions.
- Capacity exhaustion behavior: assert correct error codes, rate-limiting headers, and customer-notification signal are emitted.

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- Harness runs complete reproducibly in CI and produce a standardized JSON report that includes quantiles and autoscale events.
- For an agreed customer signature, the Dedicated pool demonstrates sustained throughput within +/-10% of promised throughput and P95 latency below the target in 4/5 independent runs.
- Autoscaler triggers validated: observed scale-up latency <= SLO defined in autoscaling doc and no flapping in step-down tests.
- Customer acceptance checklist completed and reviewed by Solutions and Product; report template approved.

Deliverables:
- Load harness code and CI job under infra/load-tests/dedicated-ramp (GitHub PR link below).
- Benchmarking playbook (Confluence) with sampling commands and report template.
- A completed run artifact for a sample mid-sized customer (include raw metrics and final PDF report).

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: harness priming could unfairly favor cache-hit scenarios. Mitigation: include both cold-start and primed runs and clearly label results.
- Risk: nondeterminism in autoscaler timing affects repeatability. Mitigation: run enough iterations and record system events to correlate.

Notes on reproducibility and customer handoff:
- Every run must record the exact model binary, hardware instance types, runtime flags, and kernel set. Lock those into the report header to avoid ambiguity.
- The customer acceptance checklist is intentionally prescriptive to avoid repeated back-and-forth during onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Harness produces machine-readable JSON report with per-quantile latencies and tokens/sec
Median of 5 runs shows sustained throughput within +/-10% of target for agreed customer signature
P95 latency target met in >=4 out of 5 runs for the sustain phase
Observed autoscale scale-up time <= documented autoscaler SLO and no scale-down flapping in hysteresis tests
Fleet fallback behaviors exercise both model-variant fallback and region fallback and produce expected controlled errors
